Callout stable

An emphasised aside inside a guide section: a typed tag (Key concept / Pro tip / Trap — a decorative glyph and a mono label in the live accent), an optional serif title, a body of rich inline content. Not interactive.

Variants: key pro trap · A11y: pass

Key / Pro / Trap are types, not states: no hover, no focus (RFC §3). Chrome lives in callout.css; the 2-column grid the site lays callouts in stays product-side (RFC §7 Q4).

RFC: Callout.rfc.md · Figma node: 61:26 · Figma docs page: 66:3

Examples

Live renders — hover and keyboard states all work here.

Key concept

Shove, then leave

Fast-push the wave with your abilities, then roam while the enemy is stuck last-hitting under their tower.
Pro tip

Priority is permission

Only roam when the enemy must choose between following you and losing CS.
Trap

Don't roam into nothing

A roam that gets no kill, no tower and no vision is just lost farm and a missed wave.
Pro tip
Title is optional: without it the tag leads straight into the body.
<Callout type="key" title="Shove, then leave">Fast-push the wave with your abilities, then roam while the enemy is stuck last-hitting under their tower.</Callout>
<Callout type="pro" title="Priority is permission">Only roam when the enemy must choose between following you and losing CS.</Callout>
<Callout type="trap" title="Don't roam into nothing">A roam that gets no kill, no tower and no vision is just lost farm and a missed wave.</Callout>
<Callout type="pro">Title is optional: without it the tag leads straight into the body.</Callout>

Guidelines

Golden rules

  1. Key concept: the one takeaway. The single most important thing to retain from a section. Maximum one per section, placed first.
  2. Pro tip: actionable, follows the key. Practical advice that follows from the Key concept. Several per section are fine.
  3. Trap: short, direct, no hedging. A common low-Elo mistake and why it costs. Name the symptom, then the fix.

Do

  • Put one Key concept per section, first in the grid.
  • Write the title as a short sentence; the tag already says the type.
  • Keep the body to two or three sentences; bold the one phrase to remember.

Don't

  • Don't use a Callout outside a guide section — it is not a generic card.
  • Don't write the title in capitals; the tag is the only uppercase element.
  • Don't make the body a bare link or a list — that is another component.

The 5 accents

Each tile scopes the accent axis with data-accent on the tile itself — the element-scoped theme contract.

Props

PropTypeDefaultOptionalNote
type "key" | "pro" | "trap" — no required, no fallback (RFC §7 Q5); selects the tag label and glyph
title string — yes optional serif title; absent → no <h3> is rendered
children ReactNode — no the body: rich inline content (bold, glossary terms)

Accessibility pass

Semantic structure
<article> holding, in order, the tag (plain text: Key concept / Pro tip / Trap — the type's meaning), an optional <h3> under the section's <h2>, and the body. No ARIA role overrides; the uppercase tag is CSS text-transform, AT reads the author's casing.
Keyboard
Nothing to do: no interactive element inside the component. Interactive children (glossary terms) keep their own semantics, product-side.
Decisions
The glyph (diamond / circle / triangle, 10px) is decorative — aria-hidden, no alternative text, the label already says it (RFC §7 Q3). Contrast is computed by the gate from resolved tokens: accent/default on surface/default (tag), fg/dim on surface/default (body), fg/default on surface/default (title, bold).
Notes
Implemented per RFC §4; this status moves to pass only through the accessibility engine gate, never by assertion.
